name: Bounded overseas-labour control context for IT-worker management

attribution.legal_posture: Official OHCHR overseas-labour context. Criminal adjudication is outside this context, and the described conditions apply at report scope rather than universally to every DPRK IT worker.

caveats: Most detailed testimony in the 2024 OHCHR report concerns overseas labour generally, including non-IT sectors; conditions, deductions, controls, and percentages require source-specific support before applying them to an IT worker.
This record retains no protected witness identifier or other interview-level personal data.
Use this context only for system safeguards; demographic, nationality, language, geographic, socioeconomic, and student-status screening fall outside this use.

statements: OHCHR's 2024 thematic report describes a general overseas-labour model in which host employers pay DPRK-affiliated companies, workers receive a limited share after State and living-cost deductions, and compensation can remain subject to manager discretion.
The same report describes surveillance and movement or information controls by Ministry of State Security officers or unit heads in overseas labour settings.

A/80/149 separately places information-technology workers within the broader State overseas-labour system, but the detailed 2024 testimony concerns overseas labour generally and cannot be silently transferred to every IT worker.

sources.support: Supports the narrower bridge that information-technology workers are part of the broader State-managed overseas labour system; it does not make every general labour condition IT-worker-specific
Supports the bounded general overseas-labour context concerning company-level payment collection, deductions, manager discretion, surveillance, and movement or information controls
sources.locator: OHCHR Forced labour, paras. 95-103 (report pp. 37-41; PDF pp. 39-43)
